subject.title: Export installed agents as grouped Claw packages

question: Should experimental Claw export require healthy exact installed state by default, with any partial/drifted output deferred to an explicit snapshot mode?
rationale: The implementation chooses an interoperable package contract, but the review discussion identifies materially different user expectations for reproducible operating roles versus diagnostic snapshots; that policy cannot be resolved safely from code review alone.

options.title: Adopt exact-state export
options.body: Keep healthy, complete, corroborated installed state as the only default export contract and defer snapshot output to a separately specified follow-up.

options.title: Add snapshot mode now
options.body: Define an explicit snapshot flag and machine-readable drift/lineage report before accepting partial or drifted exports.

options.title: Pause the export slice
options.body: Hold this PR until the RFC or lifecycle stack specifies the long-term package portability contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt exact-state export
recommendation.body: Keep healthy, complete, corroborated installed state as the only default export contract and defer snapshot output to a separately specified follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review comment supplies the clearest item-specific product boundary for exact-state versus snapshot behavior.
